name: The Silt Markets (Flooded Lower Shelf Bazaar)
description: A rotating ghost market that sets up in the partially-flooded sub-levels of the Lower Shelf — specifically in the drowned infrastructure corridors beneath Districts 3 through 9 — operating from flat-bottomed salvage rafts lashed together into temporary floating bazaar islands. Goods sold include unregistered geneware grafts, pre-Consolidation artifacts recovered from flooded Old Chicago basements, and black-market water filtration tech that predates the Aqua-Plex monopoly. The Silt Markets move location every 48 hours, announced only through a waterproofed paper note system called Drift Cards, which are passed hand-to-hand — deliberately analog to avoid BCI intercept. The markets have been running continuously since 2197, surviving three major corporate sweep operations by the Aqua-Plex enforcement arm.
cultural_impact: The Silt Markets are one of the primary sources of unregistered medical goods for Shelf residents who cannot afford licensed clinics, making them simultaneously a lifeline and a legal hazard — anyone caught buying there faces mandatory rehabilitation processing under Aqua-Plex jurisdiction. The Drift Card system has inspired similar analog communication networks in other Shelf districts.
key_figures: Marisol Anand-Ferreira (market coordinator, known only by raft sigil)
Kweku Jørgensen-Obi (Drift Card printer and distributor)
Aqua-Plex Enforcement Captain Liesel Nakagawa-Ruiz (primary antagonist)
locations: The Raft Ring (flooded intersection of Drowned 5th and Old Canal)
story_hooks: A Drift Card arrives addressed to someone who has been dead for six years — and the location it names is a corridor that should be completely sealed.
Aqua-Plex has planted a mole in the Drift Card distribution chain; the characters must identify the mole before the next market night without tipping off the sweepers.

A vendor at the Silt Markets is selling pre-Consolidation data chips that contain what appears to be live BCI feeds from people who died in the flooding — and someone very powerful wants them suppressed.
